metadata.title: IoMT Patient Safety Overlay

props.name: overlay-scope
props.remarks: Specialization overlay applying to networked and programmable medical devices used in diagnosis, treatment, or patient care.

props.name: authoritative-regulation
props.remarks: Primary U.S. regulatory authority governing medical device cybersecurity and patient safety.

props.name: authoritative-regulation
props.remarks: European regulatory framework governing medical device safety and risk management.

props.name: authoritative-standard
props.remarks: Risk management standard for IT-networks incorporating medical devices.

props.name: authoritative-standard
props.remarks: Quality management system requirements for medical devices.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Patient safety overlay constraining device execution, change, command, data, and lifecycle behaviors to prevent patient harm.

metadata.remarks: The IoMT Patient Safety Overlay constrains Secure-Device foundational and control patterns to ensure cybersecurity controls, failures, or operational decisions do not introduce unacceptable patient risk. In IoMT environments, patient safety overrides availability, automation, and cybersecurity optimization.

components.title: Patient Safety Supremacy Constraint
components.description: Defines patient safety as the dominant operational priority over availability, performance, or cybersecurity optimization.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Cybersecurity controls must not compromise essential clinical performance.

components.title: Clinical Command Safety Constraint
components.description: Requires command paths to support patient-safe operation and clinical intent validation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Commands must not introduce unacceptable patient risk.

components.title: Clinical Change Safety Constraint
components.description: Constrains change introduction, updates, and configuration modifications to preserve patient safety and clinical effectiveness.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device changes must be assessed for patient safety impact.

components.title: Clinical Engineering Access Constraint
components.description: Restricts engineering and service access modes to prevent unsafe clinical manipulation.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Service access must preserve safety and quality of care.

components.title: Clinical Risk Zoning Constraint
components.description: Requires clinical risk-based segmentation of medical devices and networks.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Medical IT networks are segmented to manage clinical risk.

components.title: Fail-Safe Clinical Behavior Requirement
components.description: Defines expected behavior during cybersecurity events to preserve continuity of care and patient safety.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Medical devices must maintain safe state or degrade safely under abnormal conditions.
